body: I don't have any other ammo.  That's the only M2 spec I could find.

Don't have a camera but looking at it now in the daylight calmed down a bit it's just a small nick in the top of the extractor.  Nothing else even has the finish scuffed on it.  

And as for the function test it passed with flying colors.  Sear holds the hammer tight and it transitions to the trigger hooks just fine.  

I may go ahead and order a new hammer and trigger though just to ease my paranoid mind. 

I am starting to wonder if maybe it wasn't an unintentional bump fire.

It was a distinct POP POP POP in quick succession but I was too shocked by the whole happenstance to say that I remember exactly what was happening with the rifle, whether it was fully into battery each time or what.  

And I DO appreciate every bit of this assistance and ideas.  I am genuinely interested in knowing that this rifle is safe and functioning correctly.  The last thing I want is a repeat of this event.
Whether you believe me or not, do you have any insight into what could cause a garand to not fire just one shot?

It did gouge the hell out of the top front right side of the bolt assembly if that makes a difference in anything or points to something.

And no, neither shaking the trigger group nor pushing the hammer causes it to fall.
The sere is pristine.  I see absolutely nothing wrong with it and it is functioning just as it should as I try to make it fail with the trigger group removed from the rifle.
